items.stem: State any three benefits of international business to nations.
items.answer: Earning of foreign exchange; More efficient use of resources; Improving growth prospects and employment; Increased standard of living
items.markingKey: Any three of: Earning of foreign exchange; More efficient use of resources; Improving growth prospects and employment; Increased standard of living (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the benefits of international business to firms?
items.answer: More efficient use of resources
items.markingKey: (d) "More efficient use of resources" is one of the benefits of international business to nations, not one of the benefits of international business to firms.

items.stem: Distinguish between domestic business and international business on the basis of nationality of buyers and sellers, currency used and customer heterogeneity.
items.answer: (i) Nationality of buyers and sellers: domestic business: same country; international business: different countries. (ii) Currency used: domestic business: one currency; international business: more than one currency. (iii) Customer heterogeneity: domestic business: more homogeneous customers; international business: customers differ in language, tastes and habits.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Nationality of buyers and sellers: domestic business: same country; international business: different countries. (ii) Currency used: domestic business: one currency; international business: more than one currency. (iii) Customer heterogeneity: domestic business: more homogeneous customers; international business: customers differ in language, tastes and habits.

items.stem: A US firm gets local factories in Bangladesh to make shirts to its designs under its brand. Which mode of entry into international business is used?
items.answer: Contract manufacturing
items.markingKey: (c) Contract manufacturing. Local producers make goods to the firm's specifications.

items.stem: Mehta Brothers has spare capacity at its plant in Pune and uses it to make goods for export. Which benefit of international business is illustrated? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Increased capacity utilisation. Surplus capacity is used for export.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Increased capacity utilisation; 2 marks for the justification: Surplus capacity is used for export.

items.stem: Which mode of entry into international business is used? In each case give a reason. (i) Nair Agencies and a Japanese company set up a new firm in India, each holding 50% of its shares. (ii) Nair Agencies sets up a company in Singapore and holds all of its shares.
items.answer: (i) Joint venture: Jointly owned by two firms. (ii) Wholly owned subsidiary: 100% equity held by the parent.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Joint venture (ii) Wholly owned subsidiary

items.stem: Goyal Traders of Ranchi sells its footwear directly to buyers in Germany. (i) Which mode of entry into international business is used? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Exporting: Selling goods abroad directly is exporting. (ii) Any two of: easiest way to enter foreign markets; needs less investment; less risk to foreign investment; freight and tariffs raise cost
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: easiest way to enter foreign markets; needs less investment; less risk to foreign investment; freight and tariffs raise cost

items.stem:
Gupta and Sons, an Indian maker of water purifiers, wants to enter Europe. It has little capital and does not want to risk its money abroad, but has a well-known patented technology.
(i) Suggest two suitable modes of entry. (ii) Give one limitation of each.
items.answer: (i) Licensing its technology; exporting; contract manufacturing (any two). (ii) Licensing: licensee may become a competitor or leak secrets. Exporting: freight and tariffs raise cost. Contract manufacturing: quality may not be maintained.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Licensing its technology; exporting; contract manufacturing (any two). (ii) Licensing: licensee may become a competitor or leak secrets. Exporting: freight and tariffs raise cost. Contract manufacturing: quality may not be maintained.

items.stem: A fast-food chain lets an Indian firm run outlets under its brand and system for a fee. (i) Which mode of entry into international business is used? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Franchising: Licensing of a service brand and system. (ii) Any two of: used for services; franchisor provides brand and business system; franchisee pays a fee; strict standards are followed
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: used for services; franchisor provides brand and business system; franchisee pays a fee; strict standards are followed

items.stem: A fast-food chain lets an Indian firm run outlets under its brand and system for a fee. Which mode of entry into international business is used? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Franchising. Licensing of a service brand and system.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Franchising; 2 marks for the justification: Licensing of a service brand and system.

items.stem: Jain Stores and a Japanese company set up a new firm in India, each holding 50% of its shares. (i) Which mode of entry into international business is used? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Joint venture: Jointly owned by two firms. (ii) Any two of: jointly owned by two or more firms; shared investment and risk; access to local partner's knowledge; conflicts between partners possible
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: jointly owned by two or more firms; shared investment and risk; access to local partner's knowledge; conflicts between partners possible

items.stem: Ahuja Retail finds it can sell its electronic goods abroad at a higher price than in India. Which benefit of international business is illustrated?
items.answer: Prospects for higher profits
items.markingKey: (a) Prospects for higher profits. Higher prices abroad mean higher profits.
options: Way out of intense competition in the domestic market

items.stem: A US firm gets local factories in Bangladesh to make shirts to its designs under its brand. (i) Which mode of entry into international business is used? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Contract manufacturing: Local producers make goods to the firm's specifications. (ii) Any two of: foreign firm makes goods to the specifications of the international firm; no investment in plant; local producer gets assured business; quality may not be maintained
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: foreign firm makes goods to the specifications of the international firm; no investment in plant; local producer gets assured business; quality may not be maintained

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "IEC number"?
items.answer: The Importer Exporter Code issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade, needed for exporting or importing.

items.stem: State one difference between sight draft and usance draft on the basis of when documents are released.
items.answer: sight draft: on payment of the bill; usance draft: on acceptance of the bill
items.markingKey: 1 mark: sight draft: on payment of the bill; usance draft: on acceptance of the bill

items.stem: Explain the following steps in the export procedure: (i) Obtaining an export licence (ii) Pre-shipment inspection.
items.answer: (i) Obtaining an export licence: Including the IEC number and registration with the export promotion council. (ii) Pre-shipment inspection: Goods are inspected by an authorised agency where required.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Including the IEC number and registration with the export promotion council. (ii) Goods are inspected by an authorised agency where required.

items.stem: Sharma Industries obtains a mate's receipt and exchanges it for a bill of lading. Is it a step in the export procedure or the import procedure?
items.answer: Export procedure
items.markingKey: (a) Export procedure. The exporter gets these after loading.

items.stem: The person in charge of the carrier delivers a document to the port listing the imported goods unloaded. Which document is described? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Import general manifest. Lists goods brought in by the carrier.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Import general manifest; 2 marks for the justification: Lists goods brought in by the carrier.

items.stem: Is it a step in the export procedure or the import procedure? In each case give a reason. (i) Mishra Stores files a bill of entry and pays customs duty. (ii) Mishra Stores obtains pre-shipment finance from its bank to buy raw materials.
items.answer: (i) Import procedure: Bill of entry is filed by the importer. (ii) Export procedure: Pre-shipment finance is for exporters.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Import procedure (ii) Export procedure

items.stem:
Chopra Enterprises of Nagpur has received an order for leather bags from a buyer in Canada whom it has never dealt with before.
(i) How can Chopra Enterprises protect itself against non-payment? (ii) Name the documents it will get after loading the goods.
items.answer: (i) Ask for a letter of credit from the importer's bank. (ii) Mate's receipt from the ship's officer, then the bill of lading from the shipping company after paying freight.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Ask for a letter of credit from the importer's bank. (ii) Mate's receipt from the ship's officer, then the bill of lading from the shipping company after paying freight.

items.stem:

items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Ask for a letter of credit from the importer's bank. (ii) Mate's receipt from the ship's officer, then the bill of lading from the shipping company after paying freight.

Under a usance draft, documents are released only on payment.

items.stem: What is meant by "Advance authorisation scheme"?
items.answer: A scheme that allows duty-free import of inputs needed to make goods for export.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A scheme that allows duty-free import of inputs needed to make goods for export.

items.stem: State one difference between special economic zone and export-oriented unit on the basis of export obligation.
items.answer: special economic zone: units must earn net foreign exchange; export-oriented unit: unit must export its entire production except permitted domestic sales
items.markingKey: 1 mark: special economic zone: units must earn net foreign exchange; export-oriented unit: unit must export its entire production except permitted domestic sales

items.stem: Explain the following organisations set up by the government for export promotion: (i) Export Promotion Councils (ii) Commodity Boards.
items.answer: (i) Export Promotion Councils: Promote exports of particular products. (ii) Commodity Boards: Promote production and export of traditional commodities such as tea, coffee and spices.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Promote exports of particular products. (ii) Promote production and export of traditional commodities such as tea, coffee and spices.

items.stem: Goyal Brothers wants its export consignment inspected for quality before shipment. Which organisation would help?
items.answer: Export Inspection Council

items.stem: Ahuja Retail wants its export consignment inspected for quality before shipment. Which organisation would help? Justify your answer.

items.stem: State any three objectives of the WTO.

items.stem:
Malhotra Brothers of Guwahati imports raw materials to make goods for export. It also plans to buy new imported machines. Duties make its products costly abroad.
(i) Suggest two schemes that reduce its duty burden. (ii) Where could it set up a new plant for more incentives?
items.answer: (i) Advance authorisation (duty-free inputs) or duty drawback (refund); EPCG for machinery. (ii) In a special economic zone, or as an export-oriented unit.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Advance authorisation (duty-free inputs) or duty drawback (refund); EPCG for machinery. (ii) In a special economic zone, or as an export-oriented unit.

items.stem: Exports by Indian firms earn dollars that pay for oil imports. Which benefit of international business is illustrated?
items.answer: Earning of foreign exchange
items.markingKey: (d) Earning of foreign exchange. Exports bring foreign exchange.
options: Way out of intense competition in the domestic market

items.stem: Distinguish between sight draft and usance draft on the basis of when documents are released, risk to exporter, credit to importer and name of arrangement.
items.answer: (i) When documents are released: sight draft: on payment of the bill; usance draft: on acceptance of the bill. (ii) Risk to exporter: sight draft: lower; usance draft: higher. (iii) Credit to importer: sight draft: none; payment is immediate; usance draft: credit for the usance period. (iv) Name of arrangement: sight draft: documents against payment (D/P); usance draft: documents against acceptance (D/A).
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) When documents are released: sight draft: on payment of the bill; usance draft: on acceptance of the bill. (ii) Risk to exporter: sight draft: lower; usance draft: higher. (iii) Credit to importer: sight draft: none; payment is immediate; usance draft: credit for the usance period. (iv) Name of arrangement: sight draft: documents against payment (D/P); usance draft: documents against acceptance (D/A).

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "National treatment"?
items.answer: The principle that imported goods, once they enter a market, are treated no less favourably than domestic goods.
items.markingKey: (a) National treatment: The principle that imported goods, once they enter a market, are treated no less favourably than domestic goods.
options: The principle that imported goods, once they enter a market, are treated no less favourably than domestic goods.
The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, signed in 1947, which governed world trade before the WTO.
The WTO Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights.
The principle that any trade advantage given to one member must be given to all members without discrimination.

items.stem: Das Traders obtains a mate's receipt and exchanges it for a bill of lading. Is it a step in the export procedure or the import procedure? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Export procedure. The exporter gets these after loading.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Export procedure; 2 marks for the justification: The exporter gets these after loading.

items.stem:
Ishaan, a new importer in Dehradun, wants to import machinery from Italy and asks you the steps after the goods are shipped.
(i) List the steps. (ii) Which document is filed for customs clearance? (iii) What must he have before importing at all?
items.answer: (i) Receipt of shipment advice, retirement of import documents, arrival of goods, customs clearance and release of goods. (ii) Bill of entry. (iii) An IEC number (import licence) and foreign exchange arranged through a bank.
items.markingKey: 6 marks: (i) Receipt of shipment advice, retirement of import documents, arrival of goods, customs clearance and release of goods. (ii) Bill of entry. (iii) An IEC number (import licence) and foreign exchange arranged through a bank.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the benefits of international business to nations?
items.answer: Prospects for growth
items.markingKey: (b) "Prospects for growth" is one of the benefits of international business to firms, not one of the benefits of international business to nations.

items.stem: Goyal Retail sets up a factory near Coimbatore that undertakes to export its entire output in return for incentives. Which export promotion scheme or facility is used? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Export-oriented unit. EOUs export their entire production.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Export-oriented unit; 2 marks for the justification: EOUs export their entire production.

items.stem: What is meant by "WTO"?
items.answer: The international organisation, set up on 1 January 1995 as successor to GATT, that lays down and administers rules for trade between nations.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: The international organisation, set up on 1 January 1995 as successor to GATT, that lays down and administers rules for trade between nations.
